tagline: South America's food capital layers pre-Inca pyramids, colonial balconies and cliff-top neighbourhoods over a Pacific coastline where surfers ride below the high-rises. It is ranked #36 on Time Out's Best Cities 2026 list.
overview: Founded in 1535 as the seat of Spanish power in South America, Lima was the richest city in the Americas for two centuries. The colonial centre, with its wooden balconies and the vast Plaza Mayor, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Modern Lima runs on food. It is the only city with two restaurants in the world's top 10, and ceviche — raw fish cured in lime and chilli — is a national obsession. Miraflores' cliff-top promenade looks down on surfers, paragliders and the 1,500-year-old adobe pyramid of Huaca Pucllana right in the neighbourhood.

Boho Barranco fills with street art, craft-beer bars and the Bridge of Sighs, while Callao's port districts have become a gallery scene in their own right. Day trips reach the ancient ruins of Caral — the oldest city in the Americas — or the desert oases and penguin islands of the coast.

funFacts.title: THE GASTRONOMY CAPITAL
funFacts.text: Lima is home to two of the world's top ten restaurants and is widely called South America's food capital.

funFacts.title: A PYRAMID DOWNTOWN
funFacts.text: The 1,500-year-old adobe pyramid of Huaca Pucllana sits surrounded by Miraflores apartment blocks.

funFacts.title: THE CITY OF KINGS
funFacts.text: Founded in 1535, Lima was the capital of Spanish South America for nearly 300 years.

funFacts.title: IT ALMOST NEVER RAINS
funFacts.text: Lima is one of the driest capitals on Earth — a grey coastal fog called garúa provides most of its moisture.

funFacts.title: CEVICHE MASTERS
funFacts.text: Peru's national dish is protected by law, and Lima's cevicherías serve it at lunchtime only, the traditional way.

funFacts.title: THE OLDEST CITY IN THE AMERICAS
funFacts.text: Caral, about three hours north, is a 5,000-year-old city as old as the pyramids of Egypt.

funFacts.title: A BRIDGE OF SIGHS
funFacts.text: Barranco's wooden Bridge of Sighs is said to grant a wish if you cross it holding your breath.

funFacts.title: PENGUINS NEARBY
funFacts.text: The Palomino Islands off the coast host sea lions and Humboldt penguins.

funFacts.title: CHINOS AND CRIOLLOS
funFacts.text: Lima's Chinatown is one of the oldest in the Americas, born of 19th-century migration.

funFacts.title: A MIRACLE PAINTING
funFacts.text: The city's Lord of Miracles procession is one of the largest Catholic processions in the world.
